chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḍurays, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two knowledges: a knowledge disclosed and a knowledge withheld. As for the disclosed, there is nothing from what the angels and the messengers know except that we know it. And as for the withheld, it is that which is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the Mother of the Book; when it emerges, it takes effect.”

key_terms.أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ: the Mother of the Book, the supreme divine register with Allah
key_terms.الرُّسُلُ: the messengers entrusted with divine knowledge
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who receive divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.عِلْمَيْنِ: two categories of knowledge attributed here to Allah, Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.مَكْفُوفٌ: withheld or restrained knowledge kept back
key_terms.نَفَذَ: it takes effect or is carried through when it comes forth

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the Imams’ knowledge and the knowledge that remains exclusively with Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between two categories of divine knowledge: one disclosed to the angels and messengers, and another retained uniquely with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It emphasizes the vast knowledge granted to the Imams concerning revealed matters, while affirming that a concealed level of knowledge remains in Allah’s exclusive possession in the Mother of the Book.
